title: AtlasVLA: Giving a Robot Policy a Memory of Where It Is and What It Has Done
hook: A wrist camera forgets an object the moment it leaves frame. AtlasVLA keeps a persistent 3D map plus a record of task progress — and beats multi-view baselines with one camera.
key_points: Diagnoses two failure modes of reactive vision-language-action models: perception forgetting when objects leave the camera's view, and task-progress forgetting during multi-step execution.
Answers both with a dual memory: a 4D Persistent World State Memory and an Ego-Working State Memory.
The world memory lifts transient 2D observations into a globally updated, voxel-hashed spatial state, so blind spots are filled from what was seen earlier.
The ego memory tracks historical ego state and how far along the task is, so multi-step plans do not restart from scratch.
A diffusion transformer policy is conditioned on the joint World-Ego state, turning reactive control into proactive spatial reasoning.
Using only a wrist camera it reports absolute success-rate gains of 9.4% on LIBERO-Long and 17.5% on real-world long-horizon tasks, outperforming multi-view baselines.
content_html:
Vision-language-action models drive a robot by mapping what the camera sees right now to the next action. That reactive framing breaks down in two ways, argue Guiyu Zhao and colleagues: with only a wrist-mounted camera, an object effectively ceases to exist once it leaves the field of view, and over a long multi-step task the model loses track of how far it has already gotten.

AtlasVLA attacks both with memory. A 4D Persistent World State Memory lifts each transient 2D observation into a globally updated, voxel-hashed spatial state, so earlier views keep filling in today's blind spots. An Ego-Working State Memory separately tracks the robot's own state history and task progress. A diffusion transformer policy is then conditioned on this joint World-Ego state. Evaluated on LIBERO, RLBench, and real-world benchmarks with a wrist camera alone, the authors report it beating multi-view baselines, with absolute success-rate improvements of 9.4% on LIBERO-Long and 17.5% on real-world long-horizon tasks.
extra_html: The transferable idea is that a lot of "the model can't see it" is really "the model didn't remember it." Separating spatial memory (where things are in the world) from ego memory (what I have already done) gives a policy two very different things it needs to carry forward, rather than trying to squeeze both into a context of recent frames. Full architecture and benchmark details are in the paper linked via the source.

related.title: RynnWorld-4D: RGB-Depth-Flow World Models for Robot Manipulation
related.hook: A robot needs to know how a scene's 3D structure will move, not just what it looks like. This world model predicts RGB, depth, and optical flow together, then hands the result straight to a policy.

related.title: Capek 0.5: Organizing an Embodied VLM Around Execution
related.hook: Robot execution keeps changing what needs perceiving. Capek 0.5 groups embodied skills by their role in that loop, trains a specialist for each, then merges them into one model.

related.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
related.hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

flashcards.prompt: What two kinds of forgetting does AtlasVLA say reactive VLA models suffer from?
flashcards.back_html: Perception forgetting — objects vanish from the model's world once they leave the wrist camera's field of view — and temporal task-progress forgetting during multi-step execution.

flashcards.prompt: How does AtlasVLA let a single wrist camera cover visual blind spots?

choices.text: It lifts 2D observations into a globally updated, voxel-hashed 3D world state that persists across time
It adds a second camera view and fuses the two streams
It re-runs the whole video history through the encoder at each step
It asks a language model to describe what is probably out of frame

flashcards.explanation_html: The 4D Persistent World State Memory accumulates past observations into a voxel-hashed spatial state, so a region seen earlier stays available after it leaves the current frame.

flashcards.prompt: What is the policy in AtlasVLA conditioned on, and why does that matter?
flashcards.back_html: A diffusion transformer conditioned on the joint World-Ego state — spatial memory plus task progress. That joint conditioning is what shifts it from reactive manipulation to proactive spatial reasoning.
